skill.name: error-resolver
skill.description: Diagnoses software errors with structured classification, root-cause analysis, language patterns, and reusable solution records.
skill.summary: Guides systematic debugging and records reusable fixes for recurring software errors.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The package is a Markdown troubleshooting skill, and most static hits are examples or diagnostic snippets rather than executable malware. Several recommendations still create real operational risk because they use sudo, weaken TLS validation, grant Docker access, or suggest broad permissions and destructive recovery commands.

remediation.issue: Privileged host commands appear in troubleshooting steps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and prefer least-privilege alternatives before sudo, usermod, systemctl, or Docker group changes.
Replace chmod 777 guidance with scoped ownership and minimal mode examples such as owner-only write permissions.

remediation.issue: TLS verification disabling is shown as a development workaround.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this workaround or mark it as a last resort with local-only scope and safer CA certificate guidance.

remediation.issue: Debug commands can expose environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to inspect only named non-secret variables and never paste tokens or full environment output.

remediation.issue: Destructive Git recovery commands are suggested without a confirmation gate.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings, dry-run checks, backups, and user confirmation before reset, clean, force push, or similar destructive commands.

content.value_statement: Debugging complex errors wastes time and can lead to unsafe fixes. This skill guides structured diagnosis, root-cause analysis, and reusable solution records.
actual_capabilities: Classifies errors by type, severity, scope, and origin.
Extracts key details from stack traces and error messages.
Matches common patterns for Node.js, Python, React, databases, Docker, Git, networks, Go, and Rust.
Uses 5 Whys analysis to identify likely root causes.
Suggests immediate fixes, proper fixes, verification steps, and prevention steps.
Defines a replay format for recording successful error solutions.
limitations: It does not run diagnostics unless the host agent chooses to execute commands.
Some suggested commands require user confirmation and local environment knowledge.
It cannot guarantee a fix without the full error, context, and relevant code.
Replay records depend on accurate manual summaries of solved incidents.

use_cases.title: Debug Backend Exceptions
use_cases.description: Classify a server error, isolate likely causes, and plan verification steps before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Resolve Frontend Runtime Errors
use_cases.description: Compare React, browser, and API symptoms with known patterns and safer prevention steps.

use_cases.title: Document Recurring Fixes
use_cases.description: Record solved incidents as replay entries so teams can reuse known fixes faster.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner diagnosis for a pasted error.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this error: [paste error]. I was trying to [goal]. Classify it and list the safest first checks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze A Stack Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this stack trace and context: [details]. Identify the error signature, likely root cause, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Fix Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced selection between quick and durable fixes.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this recurring error: [details], compare an immediate fix, a proper fix, risks, and prevention steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Replay Entry
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced knowledge capture after resolving an incident.
prompt_templates.prompt: We solved this error: [summary]. Create a reusable replay record with signature, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention.

output_examples.input: A Node.js app fails after cloning because a dependency cannot be found.
output_examples.output: The skill classifies the issue as a dependency error, checks installation state, recommends reinstalling project packages, and adds setup prevention notes.

output_examples.input: A React component updates state after it has unmounted.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies an async cleanup problem, recommends cancellation or mounted-state tracking, and records a replay tag for future matches.

output_examples.input: A database client reports a local connection refused error.
output_examples.output: The skill separates service availability, host, port, and credential causes, then proposes safe status checks before configuration changes.

best_practices: Provide the full error message, stack trace, and recent change history.
Ask for verification steps before applying any command or code change.
Record successful fixes only after confirming the error no longer reproduces.
anti_patterns: Do not run privileged or destructive commands without explicit review.
Do not paste secrets, private keys, or full environment dumps into prompts.
Do not reuse a replay record when the error context differs materially.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps classify, analyze, fix, verify, and document software errors across common development stacks.

faq.question: Does it execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance. Any command execution depends on the host agent and should require user approval.

faq.question: Can it analyze stack traces?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts error type, file location, call depth, and likely root cause from stack traces.

faq.question: Which technologies are covered?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for Node.js, Python, React, databases, Docker, Git, networks, Go, and Rust.

faq.question: What is the replay system?
faq.answer: Replay records store solved error signatures, causes, fixes, verification steps, and prevention notes for future reuse.

faq.question: What should I avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, tokens, private keys, full environment dumps, and sensitive customer data.
